The paper calls itself "visual RAG", but it retrieves images and takes a majority vote over their labels. No language model conditions its output on retrieved text, so it does not fit the RAG definition, and it is image-only (multimodal-only, E9) in any case. Two exclusion codes could apply:

- **E1:** retrieval without a generator conditioning on the retrieved content.
- **E9:** the work is purely visual, so it falls under multimodal-only RAG.

E9 is the more explicit fit, since the paper itself describes the method as visual RAG. E1 is also defensible because there is no generator at all. I choose E9 because it matches the paper's own framing.

{"decision":"EXCLUDE","code":"E9","reason":"Visual-only retrieval for image classification via majority vote; no text generator conditioning; multimodal/visual RAG."}
